rationale: The Latin anchors *ascendere* (ascendunt montes, ascendit ad Dominum, ascende cacumen Phasgæ montis) all point to literal upward movement — climbing mountains or ascending to a height — which maps directly to ascend.v.01 ("travel up"). The sibling gloss "to go in any direction" (covering *descendere* as well) confirms the root sense is physical travel, and the primary directional sense here is upward.
